claims.text: Actively learned Moment Tensor Potentials have been applied in refractory Mo-Nb-Ti-Ta multi-principal-element alloys.
MTPs demonstrated in solid-state refractory alloys are transferable to liquid Ta-based refractory HEAs near melting.
Thermodynamic integration has O(N^3) scaling that can be bypassed by the proposed perturbation scheme.
A Bayesian active-learning loop can restrict DFT sampling to the most informative liquid configurations near the melting point.
An MTP trained on a sparse DFT dataset of liquid configurations can support accurate free-energy perturbation in a Ta-based HEA.
The perturbation scheme can exploit a smooth learned potential-energy surface instead of performing full thermodynamic integration.
Liquid short-range order and local coordination environments are the primary drivers of free-energy differences in multicomponent liquids.
The MTP descriptor space captures the relevant liquid short-range order and local coordination environments.
The free-energy landscape of the liquid is dominated by local structural motifs.
Active learning allows the MTP to map the liquid potential-energy surface without the exhaustive sampling required by thermodynamic integration.
The learned potential is computationally cheaper than DFT while being more accurate than classical EAM for complex multicomponent liquid structures.
Existing TOR-TILD or similar methods fail in multicomponent spaces because of a curse of dimensionality in their training sets.
Uncertainty-directed active learning mitigates the multicomponent training-set dimensionality problem more effectively than uniform sampling.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10 to 100 relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method will predict melting temperature with an error below 50 K.
The method will resolve subtle free-energy differences between competing liquid structures in the Ta-based system.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the relevant complex liquid structure in the Ta-based system.
The method is valid when the liquid potential-energy surface is relatively smooth and dominated by short-range interactions.
Directional bonding or magnetic ordering omitted from the training set can cause the method to fail.
Incomplete coverage of liquid coordination environments can produce extrapolation errors and systematic free-energy bias.

contradictions.description: The predicted accuracy is less than 50 K error, but falsification requires error greater than 100 K. Results between 50 K and 100 K would violate the predicted outcome without falsifying the hypothesis.

The baseline conflates ab initio molecular dynamics with EAM or classical-potential simulations. AIMD obtains forces electronically rather than using an EAM potential, although EAM may separately serve as a thermodynamic-integration reference.
